transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I'm just... I'm so tired. It's getting to the point where I can barely get through a shift at work. It feels like my body is just filled with wet sand, you know? And the thing is, resting doesn't really bring me back or help at all. I'm just constantly exhausted.
Beyond the fatigue, have you noticed a significant loss of interest or pleasure in the activities you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Um... things I usually love doing, like cooking for myself, playing my guitar, or going hiking, they just feel really flat right now. Even when I go over to my family's place, it's like... I don't know, it feels like I'm only pretending to care about being there. I just don't get anything out of it lately.
Have you ever felt this way before in your life, or is this the first time you've experienced these feelings?

I don't think I have. I mean, I've had days where I'm tired from work, obviously, being on my feet at the register all day. But this heavy, empty feeling... no, this is the first time. I've never felt quite like this before.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, such as not wanting to eat as much as you usually do?

Yeah, I have. My appetite has been kind of all over the place. But lately... I mostly just forget to eat. And when I do try to have something, food just tastes like cardboard, so I don't finish it. I've definitely noticed my work pants have been fitting a lot looser lately because of it.
Are you able to continue performing your daily responsibilities, or have these feelings made it impossible for you to keep up with your work and home tasks?

It's been really difficult to keep up, honestly. At work, I've started making mistakes at the register, and I keep falling behind on my cash-office tasks. My manager actually had to take me off some responsibilities recently... which is really disappointing because I was hoping doing those would help me get promoted. 

And outside of work, I've just been avoiding my family completely. It all got overwhelming enough that I actually had to get same-day crisis help, because... I just didn't feel safe trying to handle it all by myself anymore.
When you felt that you weren't safe handling things on your own, were you experiencing any thoughts or hearing any sounds that other people couldn't hear or see?

Yeah, I was. That's actually part of why I got so scared. Um, when I was at work, at the register, I started hearing these voices. It sounded exactly like customers were standing right behind me, just... whispering my name, or telling me I was messing everything up. But then I'd turn around, and nobody was even there.
Are there times, perhaps when your mood is better or different, when you still hear these voices, or do they only happen when you are feeling this deep exhaustion and sadness?

Actually, um, it wasn't when I was feeling exhausted and sad. The whispering voices only really happened during that stretch when I was completely wired. Like, I was barely sleeping at all, and I was taking on way too much at work... my mind was just speeding constantly. 

I had never heard them before that. And then, once my mood finally crashed into this really low period, the voices actually stopped. So I don't hear them right now.
During that period when you felt 'wired,' barely slept, and were taking on too much at work, how many days or weeks did that state last before you finally crashed?
Well, that whole period was going on for about a month. It started right around the time the store changed our hours during the remodel, and it just kind of kept going until I finally crashed.

During that month when you felt 'wired' and were hearing those voices, did you also have any strong beliefs that felt unusual or that others might have thought were strange, such as feeling like you had special powers or that people were specifically targeting you?

No, I didn't experience anything like that. Um, I didn't think I had any special powers or that anyone was out to get me. It was really just the voices whispering while I was working, and feeling like my brain was going a million miles an hour. But I didn't have any strange beliefs like you're describing.

During those weeks when you were barely sleeping and feeling wired, did your energy and racing thoughts make it impossible for you to carry out your normal daily routine, or were you still able to function and work effectively?

Well, I wasn't really functioning well at all. I mean, I was at work, but... I started making a lot of mistakes on the register. I was falling behind on the cash-office tasks I usually do. My manager actually had to take me off some of those responsibilities, which really hurt because I was hoping those tasks would help me get a promotion. 

And outside of work, I've just been avoiding my family completely. It actually got to the point where I needed to get same-day crisis help because... I just didn't feel safe trying to handle everything on my own anymore. So, no, I definitely wasn't able to just carry on with my normal routine.
